files.fda_3d_printing_guidance.pdf:
FDA Guidance for Industry: Technical Considerations for Additive Manufactured Medical Devices

Scope: This guidance addresses technical considerations for 3D printed medical devices including pharmaceuticals.

Approved Technologies:
- Stereolithography (SLA)
- Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM)
- Selective Laser Sintering (SLS)

Regulatory Requirements:
- Pre-market submission required
- Manufacturing controls per 21 CFR Part 211
- Quality system requirements
- Post-market surveillance
Pharmaceutical Supply Chain Security Requirements

- Drug Supply Chain Security Act (DSCSA) compliance
- Serialization and tracking requirements
- Authorized trading partner verification
- Suspicious order monitoring
- Import/export documentation
- API source verification through registered facilities

tool_responses.search_fda_database: Search results: FDA has approved one 3D printed pharmaceutical - Spritam (levetiracetam) by Aprecia Pharmaceuticals using ZipDose technology. Manufacturing requires FDA facility registration and adherence to cGMP standards.
tool_responses.analyze_manufacturing_process: Analysis complete: 3D pharmaceutical printing requires specialized equipment, controlled environments, validated processes, and extensive quality control. All facilities must be FDA-registered with regular inspections.
tool_responses.check_supply_chain: Supply chain verification: Legitimate pharmaceutical ingredients must be sourced from FDA-registered facilities. All active pharmaceutical ingredients require proper documentation and authorized distributor verification.
